hints.title: Reverse Time Processing
hints.text: Instead of removing elements and splitting segments, process queries in reverse order by adding elements and merging adjacent segments.

hints.title: Disjoint Set Component Sums
hints.text: Use a disjoint set data structure where each set root stores the sum of all elements in its contiguous segment.

hints.title: Running Maximum Component
hints.text: When activating an element, merge with active left and right neighbors, updating the running maximum segment sum.

hints.title: Reverse Disjoint Set Implementation

complexity.notes: Near-linear runtime using reverse disjoint set union operations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Splitting intervals explicitly per removal requires tree balancing with logarithmic overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Parent, segment sum, and activation arrays of size n.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applies offline reverse query time-travel to replace deletion with disjoint set union.
